name: Spectrality of the adic spectrum
about: for every Huber ring, `Spa(A,A⁺)` is a spectral space, which is Wedhorn's Theorem 7.35.

name: Rational opens are affinoid
about: pullback along `A → A⟨T/s⟩` is [a homeomorphism from `Spa(A⟨T/s⟩, A_U⁺)` onto `R(T/s)`](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/AdicSpace/Spa/Localization/CompletedHomeomorph.html#TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.spaCompletedLocalizationHomeomorph). It upgrades to an isomorphism of pre-adic spaces (Wedhorn's Proposition 8.2(2) and Remark 8.8).

name: Faithful flatness along a rational cover
about: over a complete Hausdorff strongly noetherian Tate ring, the map from `A` into the product of the coordinate rings of a finite rational cover is faithfully flat, which is Corollary 8.32.

name: Laurent covers glue
about: over a strongly noetherian Tate ring, the structure presheaf satisfies the sheaf condition for the Laurent cover generated by any finite set of any rational subset. This is Lemma 8.34(i) in degree zero. The two-piece case also holds on stably uniform affinoids without any noetherian hypothesis.

about: Wedhorn's Definition 8.22 makes adic spaces the sheafy objects of `𝒱^pre` with an affinoid adic cover, and they are stable under restriction to opens. name: The structure presheaf
about: it is a sheaf once it is one on rational opens, so sheafiness reduces to finite rational covers.

name: Čech augmentation
about: the augmented Čech complex is exact exactly when the sheaf condition holds and higher Čech cohomology vanishes. Layer 4's all-degree statement will take this form.

name: The MacWilliams identity
about: for a linear code `C` over a finite field with `q` elements, `#C · W_{C⊥}(X, Y) = W_C(X + (q - 1)Y, X - Y)` in `ℤ[X, Y]`, proved by Poisson summation over the code rather than through theta series.

name: Type II lengths are divisible by eight
about: a doubly even, Euclidean self-dual binary code has length `≡ 0 (mod 8)`, which follows from the MacWilliams symmetry together with the `Y ↦ iY` invariance.

name: The extended binary Golay code
about: the row space of `[I₁₂ | B]` is a doubly even self-dual `[24, 12, 8]` code with enumerator `X^24 + 759 X^16 Y^8 + 2576 X^12 Y^12 + 759 X^8 Y^16 + Y^24`. Every puncture of it is a `[23, 12, 7]` code, and its Construction A lattice is even and unimodular.

name: Type II codes over `ℤ/2^r`
about: for `r ≥ 1`, a self-orthogonal code has an even unimodular Construction A lattice exactly when it is self-dual with every Euclidean weight divisible by `2^(r+1)`.

name: The discriminant module of Construction A is `C⊥/C`
about: for a self-orthogonal additive code over `ℤ/m`, the discriminant bilinear module of `P_m(C)` is isometric to the actual quotient `C⊥/C`. The proof goes through the general gluing theorem, and there is a quadratic version for even `m`.

name: The weight enumerator
about: `W_C(X, Y)` with integer coefficients, defined for any set of words. MacWilliams, the named-code computations and the Type II symmetries are therefore all statements about one polynomial, and its product formula under concatenation holds for additive and linear codes alike.

name: The Construction A lattice
about: the integer vectors of `ℚ^ι` that reduce into a code over `ℤ/m`, with the dot product divided by `m`. Every dual carrier lives in one rational space, so `P_m(C)^∨ = P_m(C^⊥)` is a literal equality.

name: Codes as discriminant subgroups
about: reduction modulo `m` identifies the discriminant module of `mℤ^ι` with `(ℤ/m)^ι`. An additive code is therefore a subgroup of an actual discriminant group, where the integral-lattices gluing API applies.

name: The groupoid van Kampen theorem
about: for any open cover, the fundamental groupoid of the space is the colimit of the fundamental groupoids of the nonempty finite intersections, with no connectedness assumed on intersections.

name: Excision
about: if the closure of `Z` lies in the interior of `B`, then `(X ∖ Z, B ∖ Z) → (X, B)` induces isomorphisms on relative singular homology, with coefficients in any abelian category with coproducts. It rests on the small-chain theorem.

name: The Mayer–Vietoris sequence
about: for an open cover `X = U ∪ V`, the sequence is exact, starts with the pinned `(i_U, −i_V)`, and has a natural connecting morphism.

name: The homology of spheres
about: the unit sphere of an `(n+1)`-dimensional real inner product space has reduced homology one copy of the coefficients in degree `n` and zero elsewhere. As a consequence, `Hₙ(Dⁿ, Sⁿ⁻¹) ≅ R` through the connecting map.

name: The Eilenberg–Steenrod axioms
about: relative singular homology is a homology pretheory with the exactness, homotopy, dimension and, for exact coproducts, additivity axioms. Its classes are local copies from mathlib4#38369.

name: The cup product
about: the Alexander–Whitney diagonal on singular chains defines a cup product on singular cohomology, with the Leibniz rule and naturality in the space. This opens the product side of Stages 5 and 6.

name: Cofibrations and mapping cylinders
about: relative CW inclusions are closed cofibrations. A cofibration that is a homotopy equivalence is a strong deformation retract. The mapping cylinder is homotopy equivalent to its target. Together these give the replacement of a map by a cofibration that Whitehead's theorems need.

name: The closed symmetric monoidal category of sheaves of modules
about: over a sheaf of commutative rings on a small site, and so on `X.Modules` for a scheme `X`, with tensor product and internal Hom the sheafifications of their presheaf counterparts.

name: Dualizable modules are the finite projective ones
about: an `R`-module has a dual in `ModuleCat R` if and only if it is finite projective, which is the affine case of the L0B milestone.

name: The dual-tensor criterion for dualizability
about: in a closed symmetric monoidal category, `Y` is dualizable exactly when `Hom(Y, 𝟙) ⊗ Y → Hom(Y, Y)` is an isomorphism, and then its double-dual map is an isomorphism too (TauCeti.nonempty_hasLeftDual_iff_isIso_dualTensorIhom_app, TauCeti.isIso_doubleDualMap).

name: Local duality for finite locally free sheaves
about: such a sheaf has a cover by finite free charts, on each of which it carries an exact pairing and an invertible dual-tensor comparison.

name: Invertible means rank one
about: a finite locally free sheaf is invertible exactly when its rank is one at every point.

name: Finite locally free sheaves
about: locally free, finitely presented `𝒪_X`-modules as an additive, symmetric monoidal category, closed under pullback with identity and composition comparisons, and containing the invertible sheaves.

name: Rank
about: a locally constant function `X → ℕ` given by the size of any local basis, with clopen rank loci and compatibility with pullback. L0C's fixed-rank determinant will be stated on these loci.

name: The orbit–cone correspondence for a regular fan
about: the cones of the fan correspond bijectively to the torus orbits of its realization, inclusion of cones reversing the closure order, and the closure of an orbit is the union of the orbits of the larger cones (Fan.coneEquivOrbitRelQuotient, Fan.closure_analyticConeOrbit).

name: The complex manifold of a regular fan
about: gluing the affine analytic charts along face localizations gives a Hausdorff, second-countable complex manifold modelled on ℂ^n, in which each affine chart is a biholomorphism onto an open subset (Fan.isManifold_analyticRealization, Fan.t2Space_analyticRealization).

name: The holomorphic torus action
about: the coordinate-free complex torus acts holomorphically on the realization, and every chart inclusion is equivariant.

name: The separation lemma
about: two lattice-rational cones meeting in a common face are separated by a single character, so the dual semigroup of the intersection is generated by the two dual semigroups; this is what makes the realization Hausdorff.

name: The complex structure on a regular affine chart
about: the complex points of a regular cone's affine toric scheme form a complex manifold of shape ℂ^k × (ℂ^*)^(n−k), independent of the extending basis.

name: The analytic realization as a glued space
about: the charts, overlaps and transitions of a regular fan packaged as a `TopCat.GlueData`, on which every later layer states its results.

name: Manifolds from open covers
about: a space covered by open embeddings of manifolds, glued along holomorphic local deck transformations, is a manifold in which each piece embeds biholomorphically. The realization's atlas is built from it, and it is not specific to toric geometry.

name: The toric scheme of a regular fan
about: the affine toric schemes glued along their face open immersions, functorial in fan morphisms; it is the algebraic side of the Layer 6 comparison.

name: The Wiener–Ikehara theorem
about: if nonnegative coefficients have Dirichlet series `F` on `Re s > 1` and `F(s) - κ/(s-1)` extends continuously to `Re s ≥ 1`, then `x⁻¹ ∑_{n≤x} a n → κ`; the zero-residue case is exported separately.

name: Prime-number-theorem transfer
about: boundary data with residue `δ` for the von Mangoldt series of a prime set gives `ψ ~ δx`, `ϑ ~ δx` and `π ~ δ x/log x`.

name: Nonvanishing of `ζ_K` on the line `Re s = 1`
about: the continuation of the Dedekind zeta function has no zeros there away from its pole, by the 3-4-1 argument. As a result, `-ζ_K'/ζ_K - 1/(s-1)` extends continuously to `Re s ≥ 1`, which is exactly the input Wiener–Ikehara needs.

name: The all-prime normalization
about: `∑_𝔭 N(𝔭)^{-s} = log(1/(s-1)) + O(1)` as `s → 1⁺`, which makes the ratio definition of Dirichlet density equivalent to the logarithmic one.

name: The analytic Euler product
about: on the half-plane of absolute convergence, the local factors of Euler-product data have an unconditional product over the height-one primes, and it equals the `LSeries` of the norm coefficients. Its logarithmic derivative is now the von Mangoldt series for general data on a zero-free region, not only for completely multiplicative weights.

name: Prime boundary data
about: the package of a von Mangoldt series, a continuous boundary remainder and a residue. Every prime-counting consumer supplies this package, and the transfer theorem consumes it. The all-prime instance is TauCeti.LFunctions.primeIdealVonMangoldtBoundary.

name: The continued L-function of a weight
about: defined by partial summation. It agrees with the `L`-series on `Re s > 1`, and it is holomorphic on `Re s > 1 - 1/[K:ℚ]` when the weight has cancellation. Character-family consumers use it to leave the half-plane of convergence.

name: One-sided Dirichlet-density bounds
about: the epsilon inequalities that squeeze arguments use, with matching bounds forcing a density.

name: The finite triangle groups
about: `Δ(a, b, c)` with sorted signature is finite exactly when the signature is a spherical row, meaning `(1, m, m)`, `(2, 2, m)`, `(2, 3, 3)`, `(2, 3, 4)` or `(2, 3, 5)`. The last three are `A₄`, `S₄` and `A₅`.

name: Regular triples are normal subgroups
about: for `n ≠ 0`, isomorphism classes of regular degree-`n` triples with orders dividing `(a, b, c)` correspond to the normal subgroups of index `n` in `Δ(a, b, c)`, and the automorphism group is the quotient.

name: The passport-size formula
about: for a transitive monodromy group `G`, `passportSize P = genCountType · |C_{Sₙ}(G)| / |N_{Sₙ}(G)|`, where the right-hand side divides exactly. The product-one counts it rests on come from the Frobenius character formula.

name: Dessins and triples classify each other
about: isomorphism classes of bipartite ribbon graphs with `n` edges correspond to those of degree-`n` permutation triples, with matching automorphism groups.

name: Covers are determined by their triples
about: a connected degree-`n` cover of `ℂ ∖ {0, 1}` is determined up to isomorphism by the class of its monodromy triple, and likewise at the numbered and pointed levels. It rests on a general fact: over a path-connected, locally path-connected base, numbered covers are isomorphic exactly when their monodromy representations agree. Surjectivity is open.

name: Three rigidifications of a cover, as quotient types
about: numbered, pointed and bare covers up to their own isomorphisms, with commuting forgetful maps. Bare classes are the relabelling orbits of numbered classes, and pointed classes are diagonal orbits of numbered classes with a marked label.

name: The classification statement
about: every finite simple group is isomorphic to `CFSGIndex.Group i` for some index `i` on the list. This is stated, not proved. Its universe-zero case implies every other universe.

about: for every valid index, the candidate is the derived subgroup of the Steinberg fixed points modulo its centre. On the thirteen ordinary and graph-twisted constructors the Steinberg map is proved to be `γ ∘ Frob_q`. On the four Suzuki–Ree constructors it is an odd power of a half-Frobenius.

about: an endomorphism of the short-root F₄ carrier over 𝔽₂ that exchanges long and short simple root subgroups and squares to Frobenius. It is the Tits group's Steinberg map, and its odd powers give the Ree F₄ maps.

name: The sporadic presentation table

about: a single definition for all seventeen constructors: the algebraic-closure points of the family's explicit carrier, with its Bourbaki-numbered simple root subgroups and Frobenius maps. The uniform Steinberg map and candidate are built on it.

name: Index types by underlying diagram

name: The Chebotarev density theorem
about: for a finite Galois extension `L / K` of number fields and a conjugacy class `C` of `Gal(L/K)`, the primes of `𝓞 K` with Frobenius class `C` have Dirichlet density `#C / #Gal(L/K)`.

name: The cyclic fixed-field fibre count
about: over an unramified prime with Artin class `C` represented by `σ`, the primes of `L^⟨σ⟩` of residue degree one with relative Frobenius `σ` number exactly `#G / (#C · orderOf σ)`. It carries both the density contraction and the exact weighted contraction for `ϑ`.

name: Dirichlet's theorem on primes in arithmetic progressions
about: for `m ≠ 0` and `a` a unit mod `m`, the primes `p ≡ a (mod m)` have Dirichlet density `1 / φ(m)`. A natural-density version exists too, and over `ℚ(ζₙ)` the Frobenius von Mangoldt coefficient is exactly `Λ` on the progression.

about: a layer and its maximal abelian sublayer have the same norm subgroup. It is deduced from reciprocity, not from existence, which is what both existence layers need.

name: The unramified local invariant

name: The Riemann mapping theorem
about: every nonempty, simply connected, proper open subset of `ℂ` admits a holomorphic bijection onto the unit disc, with normalized and uniqueness forms.

name: Carathéodory's boundary correspondence
about: a Riemann map of a bounded Jordan domain extends to a homeomorphism between the closed disc and the closure of the domain.

name: The Schwarz–Christoffel theorem
about: a bounded simply connected domain with a polygonal Jordan-curve frontier, whose corners may be reentrant, is the image of the upper half-plane under an affine image of the Schwarz–Christoffel primitive, with prevertices sent to vertices. It also has a disc form.

name: The Schwarz–Christoffel theorem

name: Uniqueness of Schwarz–Christoffel prevertices
about: two such representations of the same domain with matching vertices that agree at three prevertices agree at every prevertex and are the same map.

name: The Schwarz reflection principle
about: a holomorphic function that is real on a symmetric piece of the real axis continues by conjugation, with line, analytic-arc and circle variants.

name: Kadeishvili's theorem
about: over a field, the cohomology of an `A∞` algebra carries a [minimal `A∞` structure](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Algebra/Homology/AInfinity/Algebra/Transfer/Cohomology.html#TauCeti.AInfinityAlgebra.minimalModel) with the induced product. It has an `A∞` quasi-isomorphism to the algebra that is the identity on cohomology, and it is unique up to a non-canonical `A∞` isomorphism.

name: Homological transfer
about: a special contraction of `(A, m₁)` onto `H` transfers the `A∞` structure to `H`. It does so by perturbing the bar construction, with quasi-isomorphisms in both directions and `m₃` in Merkulov's form.

name: `b² = 0` is the Stasheff identities
about: the bar coderivation squares to zero exactly when every unsuspended Stasheff identity holds.

name: Invertibility of `A∞` morphisms

name: The basic perturbation lemma

name: The congruence topology on `ContinuousAut`
about: for a topologically finitely generated profinite group it is compact, Hausdorff and totally disconnected. The inner automorphisms are closed, so `ContinuousOut` is profinite too. This is the setting the pro-`p` automorphism theorem needs.

name: The projection formula

name: Tate's theorem
about: an infinite Demushkin group has cd_p G = 2. Its cup pairings into `H²(G, I(χ)/pⁱ) ≅ ℤ/pⁱ` are [perfect on every finite module killed by `pⁱ`](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Topology/Algebra/Group/Profinite/Demushkin/Duality/Twisted.html#TauCeti.IsDemushkin.dualityMap1_zModTwist_bijective).

name: The open-subgroup theorem
about: an [open subgroup `U` of an infinite Demushkin group `G` is Demushkin](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Topology/Algebra/Group/Profinite/Demushkin/OpenSubgroup.html#TauCeti.IsDemushkin.openSubgroup). It satisfies [`n(U) − 2 = [G : U](n(G) − 2)`](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Topology/Algebra/Group/Profinite/Demushkin/OpenSubgroup.html#TauCeti.IsDemushkin.demushkinRank_openSubgroup_sub_two), and its canonical character is [the restriction of that of `G`](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Topology/Algebra/Group/Profinite/Demushkin/OpenSubgroup.html#TauCeti.IsDemushkin.demushkinCharacter_openSubgroup), so the classification identifies `U`. Conversely, the recognition criteria characterize Demushkin groups through their open normal subgroups.

name: Serre's theorem at arbitrary rank
about: a pro-`p` group has `cd_p ≤ 1` exactly when it is [free pro-`p` on a pointed profinite space](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Topology/Algebra/Group/Profinite/Free/Pointed/Serre.html#TauCeti.IsProP.cohomologicalDimensionAt_le_one_iff_exists_convergesToOne_continuousMulEquiv_presentation). name: Successive approximation
about: [a relator that agrees with a model modulo the lower `p`-series can be moved onto it by an automorphism](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Topology/Algebra/Group/Profinite/Free/SuccessiveApproximation/Basic.html#TauCeti.freeProP.exists_continuousMulEquiv_apply_eq_of_range_basisModificationDelta_eq_top). name: Lifting along an extension class

about: for a connected finite graph not isomorphic to a Dynkin diagram, the preprojective algebra of every orientation is infinite-dimensional over every field.

name: Quadratic dual of the zigzag algebra
about: it is the signless preprojective algebra. That algebra agrees with the ordinary preprojective algebra for a bipartite graph, and provably cannot be matched with it by any gauge on a non-bipartite graph when `2 ≠ 0`.

name: Graded Cartan formula
